title: Signal-weighted SDK intake playbook and enterprise onboarding scenarios
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Problem: We receive a high volume of SDK and client-library requests (new language bindings, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics). Current backlog is noisy: similar asks (e.g., token rotation, resumable sessions) are logged independently without a consistent prioritization signal. That slows enterprise onboarding and makes roadmap trade-offs ad-hoc.

Goal: Produce an operational playbook that (1) scores SDK intake items with a reproducible, signal-weighted rubric; (2) maps each request to one or more customer scenario profiles (compliance-heavy, low-latency realtime, offline batch embedding pipelines, platform integrators); and (3) codifies recommended deliverables (API surface, example apps, acceptance tests, telemetry).

Scope: Non-bug feature requests for SDKs and client libraries. Covers language support asks, auth/token lifecycle patterns (rotating tokens, mTLS, short-lived creds), streaming ergonomics (resume semantics, chunking, checkpointing), and onboarding docs/examples. Does not include core runtime changes or infra-only autoscaling work (those are ENG-owned).

Approach summary:
- Create a scoring rubric with 5 signals: customer ARR impact, number of customers requesting, engineering effort (estimated complexity), strategic reuse potential, and compliance/security requirement. Each signal weighted [ARR 30%, customers 20%, engineering 20%, reuse 20%, security 10%].
- Define canonical customer scenarios (Enterprise Regulated, Real-time Conversational, Batch Embedding, Integration Partner) and map requests to scenarios to clarify acceptance criteria.
- For streaming ergonomics, define two patterns as baseline: (A) resumable-session API with idempotent chunk IDs and KV sync for client-side reconnect; (B) server-side reconnect with server-managed session tokens and sequence cursors. Provide recommended default (A) for mobile/web clients, (B) for heavy-throughput platform integrations.
- For auth patterns, standardize recommended flows by customer tier: hosted API customers use rotating short-lived API keys + telemetry; Dedicated/Private customers get recommended mTLS + KMS-backed signing patterns with sample rotation scripts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Precision of scoring vs. speed: a heavier scoring model yields more defensible prioritization but increases per-ticket overhead. We propose a lightweight form (4-6 questions) to capture scores, stored in the intake form rather than requiring a full PRD.
- One-size-fits-all SDKs vs. curated bindings: building many language SDKs is costly; prefer certified bindings for top-6 languages and a community adapters program for the long tail.
- Resumable streaming complexity: client-driven resumability (idempotent chunks) is simpler to reason about but puts more burden on SDKs; server-managed cursors provide higher reliability at cost of server state. We recommend client-side idempotency for initial rollout, with an engineering spike to evaluate server-cursor as follow-up.

Deliverables (minimum viable):
- Intake form template capturing the weighted signals (url: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sdk-intake-template)
- Scoring sheet and example calculations for 6 real inbound requests
- Canonical scenario profiles doc and mapping matrix
- Two reference SDK PRs (one for Node, one for Python) demonstrating the streaming resume pattern and token rotation helper utilities (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pulls)
acceptance_criteria: Intake form live and hooked to tracker (Zapier/Form->Linear), scoring auto-calculated
Scenario profiles published and referenced in >3 onboarding checklists
Two reference PRs merged that implement resume semantics and token rotation helpers
Triage rubric used on the last 25 SDK requests and prioritization aligned with at least two sales-identified enterprise wins
